claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy is conventionally processed, coarse-grained, and contains noticeable Cr- and V-rich precipitates.
Severe thermomechanical processing using high-strain-rate deformation followed by rapid annealing can produce a uniform nanocrystalline RHEA.
Severe thermomechanical processing will reduce the density of deleterious precipitates.
Nanostructuring decreases stress concentrations in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Nanostructuring limits the nucleation and growth of precipitates.
Limiting precipitate formation reduces embrittlement.
A nanocrystalline RHEA microstructure mitigates irradiation-induced defect generation and evolution.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can have substantially greater yield strength than bulk forms.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can have improved ductility relative to bulk forms.
Severe thermomechanical processing will improve yield strength and ductility relative to conventional processing under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy can remain stable during prolonged exposure at 1100 °C.
Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys can show no detectable grain growth under heavy-ion irradiation, dual-beam irradiation, and helium implantation.
Severe thermomechanical processing will minimize grain growth relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally processed coarse-grained RHEAs have significant precipitate formation that causes inferior mechanical performance under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Heavy-ion irradiation and helium implantation are relevant exposure conditions for assessing RHEAs intended for reactor environments.
The proposed effect should apply to compositionally similar W-Ta-Cr-V-based RHEAs.
The effect may not extend to substantially different alloy compositions or to materials that cannot be processed into a nanocrystalline state.
The magnitude of the mechanical improvement and the long-term irradiation stability of the nanocrystalline structure remain unknown.
A same-alloy comparison between thermomechanically processed nanocrystalline samples and conventionally processed coarse-grained controls can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant mechanical improvement or reduced irradiation damage relative to the conventional control would falsify the hypothesis.
